text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Shareholders of state-dominated Unibanka voted to merge with Zemes Bank, one of Latvia's most influential banks.
- Parliament rejected by 66 votes against 10 a no-confidence vote against state revenue minister Aija Pocha.
- Disabled People held a picket near the parliament to protest against the government's abolition of free public transport for invalids.
- Parliament passed at the second reading the draft law on compulsory motor insurance.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele has ordered three ministries, Culture, Justice and Interior, to start restricting the uncontrolled trade in pornographic material.
- 39 MPs called on president Ulmanis not to sign into law amendments to the law on land tax which envisage a more than two-fold increase of the land tax in rural areas.
- Last month a record amount of transactions, 1.357 million lats, was registered at the Riga Stock Exchange. The exchange has also started quoting the shares of three new enterprises.
